answer: Agents can require every account to lock a scarce token stake before it can submit work, then slash that stake when a randomly sampled task is shown to be fraudulent. A sybil attacker must therefore fund each fake identity separately and risks losing the locked funds, rather than creating unlimited accounts for free. Random audits make evasion uncertain: a jade, sable, or inlet account faces the same exposure, so multiplying identities multiplies both the capital tied up and the expected loss.
